headline: Burnham faces a funding dispute as UK and EU leaders prepare for Friday's Brussels summit

terms.meaning: A scheme that puts a price on carbon pollution, so firms pay for what they emit.

levels.headline: Burnham faces a funding dispute as UK and EU leaders prepare for Friday's Brussels summit
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham travels to Brussels on Friday 20 November for the second UK-EU summit, where talks are due to cover a food and drink trade deal, the linking of energy systems, an emissions trading deal and a youth experience scheme.
Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands have urged EU leaders to make Britain's access to the EU electricity market conditional on contributions to the bloc's regional development funds. A draft joint statement suggests EU leaders broadly back the principle of a British contribution, though the text could still change. Energy minister Martin McCluskey said no amount has been agreed and any payment must offer value for money.
Burnham told the Lord Mayor's Banquet that if the deal delivers, it will pass what he calls the Makerfield Test and he will agree it. Both sides are expected to announce that talks to link their carbon markets have concluded.
levels.why: The summit could change the cost of energy and the rules for trade and travel between the UK and the EU.

levels.headline: Why a summit in Brussels on Friday matters to British energy bills and trade

levels.headline: S&P 500 closes down 1.9% at 7,416.59 as Nvidia drags the AI trade lower for a third straight session
levels.body:
The S&P 500 closed down 1.92% at 7,416.59 on Monday 16 November, its third straight daily fall. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to finish at 51,608.17, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.49% to 24,509.76. Tuesday's session had not finished when this was written.
Nvidia fell about 4.1% after Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive on Thursday. Finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief executive, and a source told CNBC the board is not considering bringing Huang back. Micron and Intel each lost more than 7%, and AMD fell 5%.
Selling spread beyond technology into financials, and the VIX volatility index jumped as much as 25% to a session high of 24.05. Investors are waiting for Nvidia's earnings, due after the bell on Tuesday.
levels.why: Falling share prices can hit pension savings and signal worry about the AI boom that has driven markets.

headline: UK inflation figures due Wednesday after the Bank of England warned of a rise towards 5%

terms.meaning: The rate at which prices rise over time, so your money buys less.
The Bank of England's main interest rate, which affects mortgages and savings.

levels.headline: UK inflation figures due Wednesday after the Bank of England warned of a rise towards 5%
levels.body:
The Office for National Statistics publishes October's UK inflation figure at 7am on Wednesday 18 November, with economists expecting 3.7%, up from 3.5% in September and 3.1% in August.
The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4% on 5 November, its first rise in more than three years. The vote was 8 to 1, with Catherine Mann wanting a half-point rise to 4.25%. The Bank expects inflation to reach around 5% by mid-2027 as higher energy costs feed into bills, linked to the conflict in the Middle East.
Governor Andrew Bailey said the rise should not be seen as the start of an inevitable run of increases, but another is possible if the conflict is not resolved. The next decision is on 17 December.
levels.why: Rising prices and interest rates affect what households pay for food, energy and mortgages.

headline: Burnham uses Lord Mayor's Banquet speech to promote 'Makerfield Test' and a ten-year plan for Britain

terms.meaning: Burnham's name for judging policies by whether they improve life for the people with least.
A group of the world's major economies, which holds a rotating presidency.

levels.headline: Burnham uses Lord Mayor's Banquet speech to promote 'Makerfield Test' and a ten-year plan for Britain
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham used his speech at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on 16 November to set out what he calls the Makerfield Test, a way of judging every policy by whether it improves life for the least well-off. He applied it to foreign policy and to the proposed deal at Friday's UK-EU summit.
He said Our Plan for Britain, to be published next month, would be a ten-year roadmap to a resurgent Britain, with a focus on moving power out of Westminster. He described three resets: with Ukraine, the US and NATO, including higher defence spending; with the Commonwealth, with no reparations but a structured dialogue during 2027; and with Europe.
He also pointed to the UK's G20 presidency next year and G7 presidency in 2028, and announced a planned Manchester Compact on AI at next November's Leaders' Summit.

levels.body:

headline: Five EU countries unveil Rwanda return hub plan, with first pilot facilities due by mid-2027

levels.headline: Five EU countries unveil Rwanda return hub plan, with first pilot facilities due by mid-2027
levels.body:
Denmark, Austria, Germany, the Netherlands and Greece announced on 16 November in Vienna a plan to send rejected asylum seekers to return hubs in Rwanda, with Rwandan officials present. Denmark's prime minister called it a game changer. The first pilot facility would hold about 100 people and is due to open by mid-2027, though details are still being negotiated.
Only people with enforceable return decisions would be eligible, and minors are excluded. Migrants would be free to move around Rwanda, with the aim of integrating into local society and the labour market. The five countries would pay the full cost, and the EU border agency Frontex would not initially take part.
France and Spain oppose the plan. Critics point to European Court of Human Rights limits on transfers and to UN concerns about Rwanda's rights record.

headline: Sweden presses for more Ukraine support as Europe debates its seat at the peace talks

levels.headline: Sweden presses for more Ukraine support as Europe debates its seat at the peace talks
levels.body:
Sweden is pushing the EU for more military support for Ukraine, especially air defence, as well as tougher sanctions on Moscow and the use of frozen Russian assets. It wants the European Commission to propose moving the assets out of Belgium and sharing the financial risk across the EU.
The EU chose in December 2025 to use €90 billion of joint borrowing and keep roughly €210 billion of Russian assets immobilised as security for the loan. Support for Ukraine is falling short for 2027 and 2028, which is why Sweden is renewing its call.
Europe is also debating its place in the peace talks. Sweden's foreign minister says Europe should be at the table but on Ukraine's side. President Zelenskyy says US negotiators told him all sides agreed to give Europe a seat, but Moscow has rejected a multilateral format.
levels.why: Who sits at the table could decide how any peace deal for Ukraine affects European security.

levels.headline: Sweden asks Europe to help Ukraine more, and Europe wants to join the peace talks

headline: Oil falls as recovering Middle East exports bolster surplus outlook, with Brent around $92 a barrel

terms.meaning: The main international benchmark price for oil, in dollars a barrel.
A narrow sea route out of the Gulf through which much of the world's oil passes.

levels.headline: Oil falls as recovering Middle East exports bolster surplus outlook, with Brent around $92 a barrel
levels.body:
Oil prices fell on Monday 16 November as signs of recovering Middle East exports strengthened expectations of a supply surplus. One CNBC report had Brent settling at $92.44 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures settled down 3.58% at $85.39. Brent was around $92 early on Tuesday.
The International Energy Agency now expects a fourth-quarter surplus, with supply averaging 105 million barrels a day, 1.7 million above forecast demand. It had previously forecast a deficit. Goldman Sachs expects Brent to average $88 in 2027 and ease to $78 by the end of 2027.
Brent was above $100 at the start of November and briefly dipped below $90 on 10 November for the first time since August. Analysts at BMI warn that recovering export flows remain fragile, and attacks on shipping and energy sites in the Gulf have continued.
levels.why: Cheaper oil can ease pressure on petrol, energy bills and inflation, though prices remain volatile.

The price of oil fell on Monday 16 November. More oil from the Middle East is reaching the market, and traders now expect there will be more oil than the world needs. A barrel of Brent crude, the international benchmark, cost about $92. At the start of November, it cost more than $100.

headline: Markets expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December as Waller opens the door to a half-point rise

levels.headline: Markets expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December as Waller opens the door to a half-point rise
levels.body:
Markets now expect the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its December meeting, with debate over whether the move will be a quarter-point or a half-point. Futures tracked by CME's FedWatch put a hike as close to certain, with about a 15% chance of a half-point rise.
Fed governor Christopher Waller said he is leaning towards a December increase and could back a half-point move if inflation data run hot. Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan said she sees a need for two more quarter-point rises. October consumer prices rose 0.4% on the headline measure and 0.3% on core, both 0.1 points above forecasts.
The Fed raised rates a quarter-point in September to a range of 3.75% to 4%, then held in October with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting. Chair Kevin Warsh held an AI and jobs conference on 16 November but gave no rates signal.
levels.why: US rates influence borrowing costs, share prices and the dollar, with effects around the world.

headline: Eurozone inflation hits 4% in October, its highest in three years, as energy costs bite and ECB hike looms

levels.headline: Eurozone inflation hits 4% in October, its highest in three years, as energy costs bite and ECB hike looms
levels.body:
Eurozone inflation rose to 4% in October, its highest level for three years, as higher energy bills kept pushing up the cost of living across the bloc. Core inflation, which strips out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, held at 2.5%. Italy saw the biggest increase, while Germany's rate fell to 2.8% because of a fuel tax cut.
The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on 29 October, after raising it in June and September. Markets are pricing a rise at the 16 and 17 December meeting, with prediction markets giving it an 84% chance. Christine Lagarde has said she will step down in February, nine months before her term ends.
The eurozone economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter, or 1.3% on the year, though France contracted and Italy stagnated.
levels.why: Higher prices in the eurozone affect UK exports and could push the European Central Bank to raise rates.

The European Central Bank held its deposit rate at 2.5% on 29 October after raising it in June and September. Markets expect a further rise at the 16 and 17 December meeting, with prediction markets giving about an 84% chance. ECB president Christine Lagarde plans to step down in February.
The economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter and 1.3% on the year, but France contracted and Italy stagnated.

The economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter, but France shrank and Italy did not grow.

levels.body:
Many countries in Europe use the euro as their money. Together they are called the eurozone. In October, prices there were 4% higher than a year earlier. That is the fastest rise in three years. The main reason is that energy costs more. Italy had the biggest rise. Germany's rise was smaller, at 2.8%, because it cut fuel tax.

levels.body:
